# Auto-instrumentation for AI agents

Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric auto-instrumentation collects telemetry data
automatically and pushes it to AI observability tools with the help of
[OpenTelemetry Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/).

The [AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/inference-gateway) and
[Model Context Protocol (MCP) sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/mcp-sidecar)
are specialized proxies that combine Envoy with a protocol-aware external
processor to generate OpenTelemetry spans for supported model and tool calls.
Applications do not need a tracing SDK, manual spans, or tracing decorators.
This approach is sometimes called zero-code instrumentation.

Refer to [Configure
auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation)
for setup instructions.

## Introduction

Network telemetry shows which services communicated and if requests succeeded.
To gain insight from [AI
observability](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability), Consul Agentic Runtime
Fabric must collect tool invocation arguments, model interaction, and the result
of the interaction when an agent invokes a tool. AI observability details travel
in application protocols, not in network span attributes.

The specialized proxies read those protocols as traffic passes through them:

- The AI Inference Gateway instruments supported model requests and responses.
- MCP Sidecars instrument supported tool calls, including tool identity,
  arguments, results, and errors, subject to content-capture policy.

For example, an agent can call the same tool with the same arguments many times
while every HTTP request succeeds. The proxy spans capture each call and its
result, so the Agentic Analytics component can assess the repetition for
[cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection) without custom
spans in the application.

Auto-instrumentation covers only traffic that passes through these proxies.
Calls that bypass the mesh and local tool execution are not instrumented. For
the full list, refer to [Limitations](#limitations).

## How auto-instrumentation works

Each proxy produces two kinds of spans, and trace context ties them into one
workflow trace.

The following diagram shows one request through a proxy and the spans it
produces.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
Agent ──traceparent──▶ [ Envoy ──ext_proc──▶ Processor ] ──▶ Model or tool
                          │                    │
                          ▼                    ▼
Trace:   entry span
         ├── egress span (Envoy)
         └── payload span (processor)   ← siblings
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

Envoy and the processor each emit a span. Both spans share the parent from the
incoming `traceparent`, so they appear as siblings under the entry span.

### Network spans

Envoy generates network spans for observed ingress and egress requests. These
spans describe the service path, request timing, and transport outcomes. Consul
supplies the proxy configuration and service connectivity.

Network observation needs HTTP-aware listeners. Opaque TCP forwarding does not
expose the HTTP headers and bodies that payload observation reads.

### Payload spans

An external processor runs alongside Envoy and receives request and response
headers and bodies through Envoy's `ext_proc` interface. It parses supported
protocols and emits a payload span for each observed AI interaction. The
processor is infrastructure, not a library that the agent or tool imports.

The reference processor returns continuation responses without modifying the
payload. It exports spans through a bounded background queue after the exchange,
so the application does not wait for trace storage.

The payload span is a separate span, not extra attributes on Envoy's span.
External processing runs before the router creates the egress span, so the
payload span and the egress span share a parent and appear as siblings in the
trace.

### Payload span sensitive data security

<Warning>

Payload spans can contain prompts, completions, tool arguments, tool results,
and delegation messages. Auto-instrumentation does not redact them. Filter or
redact sensitive data before it reaches telemetry storage or analytics
destinations.

</Warning>

Follow these guidelines to protect sensitive data when using
auto-instrumentation:

- Do not enable content-bearing capture for a workload when the deployed path
  cannot enforce filtering or redaction.
- Keep credentials, tokens, and personal data out of telemetry.
- Restrict access to and retention of the remaining evidence.
- Expect redaction to limit downstream semantic analysis, including cycle
  detection.
- Do not promote trace IDs, arguments, prompts, or results into metric labels.

### Trace context propagation

Proxies correlate observations according to the [W3C Trace Context
specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/). You must establish the
context and a sampling decision at the entry point. The reference deployment
uses an infrastructure trace-root component in front of the API gateway.

The sampling decision determines whether a request is traced. It travels as the
sampled flag, the lowest bit of the `trace-flags` field in the `traceparent`
header. For example, a `trace-flags` value of `01` means sampled and `00` means
not sampled. Make the decision once at the entry point so that every component
on the request path receives the same value.

Applications forward incoming context on downstream calls. The reference
applications forward `traceparent`, `tracestate`, `baggage`, and `x-request-id`.
This is header propagation, not instrumentation, so applications still create no
spans.

A proxy cannot infer which incoming request caused an outgoing request inside an
application. Without propagation, observations do not form one workflow trace.
In the reference processor, a missing, invalid, or unsampled `traceparent`
prevents payload-span emission.

Applications remain responsible for propagating context and for routing calls
through the mesh.

## Observed signals

The following table lists what the proxies observe for each type of interaction.
Availability depends on the protocol, the visible request and response data,
sampling, and size limits.

| Interaction | Observed evidence |
| --- | --- |
| MCP tool call | JSON-RPC method, tool name, arguments, result text, and protocol or tool errors. |
| Model inference | Model identifier, visible prompt and completion content, offered tools, requested tool calls, and usage fields in the response. |
| Agent-to-agent delegation | Supported Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol method and message content. |
| Supported HTTP API call | Request method and path, response status, and supported JSON payload information. |
| Mesh request | Service path, network timing, and transport outcomes. |

MCP payload spans use attributes such as `mcp.tool`, `mcp.arguments`,
`mcp.result.text`, and `mcp.is_error`. Inference payload spans use `gen_ai.*`
attributes. The schema is version specific, and not every attribute is available
for every provider or protocol version.

A requested tool call in a model response does not show that the agent ran the
tool. Correlate it with the actual tool request. To turn these signals into
metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs), refer to [Operational
metrics](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability#operational-metrics).

## Telemetry pipeline components

For where these components sit in a full deployment, refer to the
[Agentic Runtime Fabric architecture diagram](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture).

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Entry-point tracing | Establish or preserve trace context and the sampling decision. |
| AI Inference Gateway | Instrument supported model exchanges. |
| MCP Sidecar | Instrument supported tool exchanges. |
| Envoy | Generate network spans and deliver supported exchanges to the external processor. |
| Protocol-aware external processor | Parse visible protocol data and generate correlated payload spans. |
| OpenTelemetry Collector | Receive spans and export them to configured destinations. |
| Trace backend | Store spans and make traces queryable. |
| Span relay | Extract trace IDs and queue analysis triggers when analytics is enabled. |
| Agentic Analytics | Retrieve trace evidence and evaluate workflow behavior, including unproductive repetition. |

The reference deployment sends Envoy spans to the collector using OpenTelemetry
Protocol (OTLP) over gRPC on port `4317`. It sends processor spans using OTLP
over HTTP at `/v1/traces` on port `4318`.

The collector exports spans to Tempo and can send a copy to the span relay. The
relay queues trace IDs, not payloads, on a BullMQ queue. Analytics workers use
the IDs to retrieve the trace from storage.

## Limitations

- **Coverage**. Proxies observe only traffic that passes through them with
  readable HTTP contents. They do not observe TLS passed through as opaque
  traffic, calls that bypass the mesh, local tool execution, or operations
  inside an external provider.
- **Protocol support**. The processor must understand the protocol. Unsupported
  or opaque payloads produce network spans only.
- **Body size**. Buffered body processing adds work to the request path and
  imposes size limits. Envoy can reject oversized requests before the processor
  receives them, and fail-open external processing does not bypass Envoy's
  buffer limits. Align listener buffers, processor gRPC limits, exporter
  capacity, and storage limits.
- **Streaming**. Buffered JSON observation does not guarantee incremental
  streaming support. Validate streaming behavior separately.
- **Incomplete evidence**. Sampling, truncation, missing context, and delivery
  loss produce incomplete traces. The reference parsers mark truncated
  attributes. Do not use truncated arguments or results as complete comparison
  inputs.
- **Double counting**. One logical call can produce network, payload, and
  external-processing transport spans, and a gateway can observe the same model
  exchange on both sides. Do not count every span as a distinct call or billable
  event. External processing observes the logical exchange, not each Envoy
  retry.
- **Delivery**. A collector acknowledgement does not prove that every
  destination persisted the span. Monitor processor stream counts, skipped
  spans, export failures, dropped spans, collector queue failures, and backend
  availability.
- **Scope of evidence**. Traces do not reveal private model reasoning, prove
  task completion, establish model quality, or replace application
  authorization. Trace storage is not a complete audit ledger or a billing
  system.
